Goal: Build Google Colab-ready Jupyter notebooks for the exercises of the textbook "Programming in High Energy Particle
Physics" (C++, ROOT, Python for HEP). For EACH exercise assigned to you, create two notebooks:
  chNN/exNN_M.ipynb           student notebook (starter)
  chNN/exNN_M_solution.ipynb  worked solution
(NN = chapter number, two digits; M = exercise number; e.g. ch05/ex05_2.ipynb).

Input: ./exercises.json holds every exercise: id (e.g. "ex5-2"), the full text including its Hint and, where present, its Answer.
The full chapter HTML is in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-boraisildak-cernbox-ytu-cms-web-book/d063581d-462e-4720-a095-24f14c060857/scratchpad/build/frag/chNN.html
(read-only) if you need the book's listings or context; reuse the book's code conventions and variable names.

YOUR EXERCISES: Chapters 1, 2, 3, 4 (all exercises of these chapters)

Notebook structure (both notebooks):
1. Markdown title cell: "Exercise N.M: <title>", one line "From *Programming in High Energy Particle Physics*, Chapter N",
   and an "Open in Colab" badge:
   [![Open In Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/isildakbora/hep-programming-guide-notebooks/blob/main/chNN/<this file name>)
2. Markdown: the exercise statement (verbatim from exercises.json, with the Hint in a collapsible <details> block). The
   student notebook must NOT contain the Answer text.
3. Setup cell(s) that make the notebook run on a fresh Google Colab runtime (Python 3.11/3.12, Ubuntu):
   - pure Python work: `%pip install -q uproot awkward vector hist mplhep iminuit scipy matplotlib numpy xgboost scikit-learn` (only what is needed).
     torch is preinstalled on Colab.
   - ROOT / PyROOT / C++ macros: install ROOT through conda with condacolab:
       !pip install -q condacolab
       import condacolab; condacolab.install()   # restarts the kernel once
     then in the NEXT cell: `!mamba install -q -y -c conda-forge root` and `import ROOT`. Add a markdown note that the first
     run takes about 3–5 minutes and restarts the runtime once. Run C++ macros with `%%writefile macro.C` plus `!root -l -b -q macro.C`,
     or via `ROOT.gInterpreter.ProcessLine` / `ROOT.gROOT.ProcessLine(".x macro.C")`.
   - Pythia 8: conda-forge `pythia8` (Python bindings) in the same condacolab route.
   - Geant4: `pip install geant4_pybind` (Python bindings, heavy). Add a warning that it downloads large datasets. If the
     exercise needs a full C++ Geant4 build, provide the complete code, explain how to run it locally, and give a
     lightweight Python stand-in in Colab that is clearly labelled as such.
   - Always guard setup so re-running is harmless, e.g. `try: import ROOT except ImportError: ...`.
4. Student notebook: short guided steps (markdown), code cells with starter code and `# TODO:` markers, and small
   self-check cells (e.g. `assert` on shapes or ranges, or printing what the expected order of magnitude should be) that do
   not reveal the answer.
5. Solution notebook: the same structure with complete, working code, plots with labelled axes and units, a short
   interpretation (markdown) of the result, and the numeric answer where one exists (it must agree with the book's
   Answer text).
6. Use seeded RNGs (np.random.default_rng(42), TRandom3(42)) and keep runtimes short (< 2 minutes on Colab CPU, except
   installs). If an exercise asks for large samples, use a smaller default with a variable to scale it up.
7. Open-data exercises: use real public files by HTTPS URL only if they are small, stable and actually exist
   (e.g. CERN Open Data record files). If unsure, generate a toy dataset in the notebook and say so. Never invent URLs.

Physics and code quality: correct physics (PDG values as in the book), no invented APIs, current library versions
(uproot 5, awkward 2, hist 2, XGBoost ≥ 2, ROOT ≥ 6.30). Notebooks must be valid nbformat v4 JSON with outputs cleared
(no stored outputs) and kernelspec python3.

Also write chNN/README.md for each of your chapters: a table of exercises with their Colab links (student and solution).

Verify (run and report output):
  python3 - <<'PY'
import nbformat,glob
for p in sorted(glob.glob("ch0[1-4]/*.ipynb")):
    nb=nbformat.read(p,as_version=4); nbformat.validate(nb)
    assert all(not c.get("outputs") for c in nb.cells if c.cell_type=="code"), p
print("valid")
PY
  Then execute every SOLUTION notebook that needs only pip-installable Python packages available here:
  jupyter nbconvert --to notebook --execute --ExecutePreprocessor.timeout=300 --output /tmp/exec_check.ipynb <file>
  (skip cells that are Colab-only such as condacolab or %pip installs by running them conditionally:
   `import sys; IN_COLAB = "google.colab" in sys.modules` and only install when IN_COLAB).
  Report which solutions executed successfully, which were skipped (ROOT/Geant4/Pythia not installed locally), and why.
  Clear outputs again afterwards (the committed notebooks must have no outputs).

Constraints: create files only under ./chNN/ for your chapters; do not modify exercises.json or anything outside this folder.
Report: files created, execution results, and any exercise where Colab support is partial.
